summary.short: Draft revision of China's Internet Information Service Management Measures (2026 consultation text). Applies to internet information services in China and sets licensing, filing, content and user-account duties, plus platform, algorithm and AI-service rules; the effective date is left blank in the draft.
summary.long: Draft revision of China's Internet Information Service Management Measures (consultation text, 3 July 2026): six chapters, 94 articles, drafted by CAC with MIIT and MPS. It covers internet information services in China and, under Art. 92, overseas providers serving China. Chapter 2 requires approval from the telecommunications authority (Art. 8-9). Chapter 3 requires filing within 30 days of network connection (Art. 16) and real-name verification (Art. 19), sets content prohibitions (Art. 24-25), removal and reporting duties (Art. 27), anti-rumour measures (Art. 31), minors' protection (Art. 35) and six-month log retention (Art. 39). Section 2 imposes platform duties, including published platform rules, account credit systems, and extra obligations for large platforms (Art. 54). Section 3 covers intelligent information services: lawful training data (Art. 59), labelling of AI-generated content (Art. 60), algorithm recommendation controls (Art. 61), gig-worker algorithm rules (Art. 62) and agent services (Art. 63). Chapter 5 provides warnings, fines, suspension, closure, licence revocation and civil or criminal liability. The effective date (Art. 94) is blank; comments close 2 August 2026.

notes: Consultation draft (Art. 94 effective date left blank). Relations and entities are populated above; section_status is set to not_applicable only because the schema requires it, not because no entries were found. Article 1 cites only the Cybersecurity Law, while Art. 86 and Art. 89 name other laws; the explanatory note also refers to the Minors Protection Law and the Heroes and Martyrs Protection Law, which the operative text does not name. Entities are public bodies only; the category of providers and the large internet platform definition (Art. 90(10), 50 million registered or 10 million monthly active users) are not coded as entities. Art. 45(3) and Art. 90(5) leave the criteria for accounts of greater influence to be set later by the national network information department with other authorities. Quotes in Art. 86 and Art. 89 are partial title strings.
